9. STRUCTURAL ASYMMETRY (MANDATORY CONTEXT)
   A. v5 maximum concurrency                    : 4
   B. aria2-F maximum configured connections    : 16
   C. selection reason                          : candidate F was selected by the v2 calibration because with --min-split-size=1048576 only >=16 connections yield the intended ~16 x 1 MiB range split at the 16 MiB evaluation scale (candidates A-E yielded larger split sizes)
   D. server pacing                             : the controlled server paces each response independently at the selected rate, so additional concurrent responses increase aggregate throughput
   consequence                                  : aria2-F can exploit up to 16 independently paced responses while v5 can exploit at most 4; this compares two complete frozen configurations and is NOT a capability-matched comparison; the asymmetry is not normalized away
   observed aria2 max in-flight (mean/max)      : 15.82 / 16
   observed v5 time-weighted concurrency (mean) : 2.702

10. INTERPRETATION
   Descriptive: v5 was slower than aria2-F in all 8 tested conditions; the pooled
   geometric ratio was 2.32 with a 95% CI that excludes 1.0, and v5 was faster in
   1/240 pairs and 0/8 conditions.
   Statistical: the pre-specified claim criteria were all false; no v5-faster claim is supported.
   Structural: v5 can use at most 4 concurrent requests while aria2-F uses up to 16;
   the controlled server paces responses independently, so aria2-F can exploit up to
   16 independently paced responses. This is a comparison of two complete frozen
   configurations, NOT a capability-matched comparison. The ratio must not be read as
   an algorithmic effect isolated from this asymmetry.
   Supported conclusion (exactly): under the tested controlled conditions at 16 MiB with
   the frozen configurations and methodology, v5 did not outperform aria2-F and was
   slower; no universal, consumer-network, optimality, convergence, or generalization
   claim is made.

11. V5 ADAPTATION CONTEXT (established before this comparison; unchanged)
   v5 passed the live technical/reaction gates and was non-constant, but adaptation
   was shallow: it generally ramps to C3-C4, never holds low concurrency, and does not
   reliably track the simulator's static optimum. The head-to-head evaluated the
   frozen candidate; nothing was retrained or tuned based on these results.
